stimulus:
In the coffee house of Edward Lloyd, shipowners seeking cover would pass a slip
around the room, and each underwriter willing to take part of the risk wrote his
name beneath the terms and the share he would bear. The lead underwriter set the
rate; the others followed or declined. A ship posted as missing was announced by a
single stroke of the Lutine bell, and two strokes marked her safe arrival, so that
everyone in the room learned the news at the same instant.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Slip-style sequential occupancy mapping of AP-1 co-binding
ideas.description: After a transient stimulus (e.g., TPA, serum, or a stress signal), profile FOS/JUN family members, the pioneer partner, and chromatin accessibility (CUT&RUN/ATAC) over days to weeks. The aim is to see whether AP-1 'signatories' accumulate on the same enhancers and whether the lead factor's early binding predicts later accessibility and H3K27ac, as in a slip where followers join the lead underwriter. Persistence of sites after AP-1 levels return to baseline would indicate a memory-like state.

ideas.title: Acute degron depletion at defined times after stimulus
ideas.description: Use dTAG/AID degrons on c-Jun, c-Fos, or JunB to remove AP-1 either during the stimulus or after it has ended, then measure the primed transcriptional response to a second stimulus. If memory requires AP-1 only at induction, the enhancer state persists after removal. If it requires AP-1 continuously, the memory collapses once AP-1 is removed. This separates AP-1 as the writer of memory from AP-1 as the carrier of memory.

ideas.title: Single-cell paired readout of AP-1 dynamics and re-stimulation response
ideas.description: Combine live-cell reporters for FOS/JUN activity (or a knock-in fluorescent tag) with a prime–rest–restimulate protocol, followed by single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC). Test whether the history of AP-1 activity in each cell, such as its amplitude and duration, predicts that cell's secondary response, and whether the memory is binary across cells (like the all-at-once bell signal) or graded.

ideas.title: Enhancer-specific causal perturbation of AP-1 motifs
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base editing or saturation mutagenesis of AP-1 motifs at primed enhancers, together with dCas9-KRAB or dCas9-based eviction, applied before or after priming. Measure whether the motif is required for establishing the open state, for keeping it, and for faster re-induction of the linked gene. Compare with other motifs to show that the memory is attributable to AP-1 sites specifically.

ideas.title: Memory kinetics and heritability across cell divisions
ideas.description: Track primed chromatin state (accessibility, histone marks, nascent transcription by PRO-seq) in lineages after stimulus washout, with time-lapse lineage tracing or sorted daughter cells across multiple divisions. Fit decay models and test whether AP-1-dependent states are inherited through mitosis (by mitotic-chromatin CUT&RUN for AP-1 bookmarking) or are rebuilt each cycle. Compare half-lives with and without AP-1 perturbation to quantify its contribution to memory.
